title: Balanced total influence lower bound
statement: Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a function on the uniform Boolean cube with $n>0$ and $\mathbb Ef=0$. Then $I(f)\ge1$. For a real cube function $h$, define $I_i(h)=\tfrac14\mathbb E_x(h(x)-h(x^{(i)}))^2$, where $x^{(i)}$ flips coordinate $i$ and $\mathbb E_x$ is uniform expectation, and $I(h)=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}I_i(h)$.
replaced: If $f$ takes values in $\{-1,1\}$, $\E[f] = 0$ and $n > 0$, then $I[f] \ge 1$.
